title: I spent 2 years building an arena FPS in Unreal Engine 5.9 and used Claude to help bring it together. What do y'all think?
author: EthernetNoswag
selftext:
Yo-Yo!

I've been working on High Rollers, a frantic arena FPS inspired by Smash Melee, Apex Legends, and BioShock Infinite. It's been a passion project for the past two years.

As creative director, I've drawn inspiration from Masahiro Sakurai, Ken Levine, and Mike Pondsmith. I've spent those two years developing the game's vision, writing a 50+ page Game Design Document, and collaborating with talented artists, animators, programmers, and sound designers. I've also worked on the VFX, materials, and shaders to give the game its signature Nintendo 3DS-inspired visual style.

Life's been lifing. Most of the artwork was already completed, but I honestly wasn't sure I'd finish a playable demo anytime soon until Claude Code and Unreal Engine 5.9 came along. 

I used Claude Code to help develop and troubleshoot gameplay systems in Unreal, including grappling, movement mechanics, and combat interactions. It's helped me turn years of design work into something playable.

I recently submitted the proof of concept to the 2026 Epic MegaJam.

There's still plenty to polish, but the demo is playable with restricted access.

What do y'all think?
